item.title: In China, Battle Is Raging for the Soul of Tibet
item.description: On the edge of the Himalayas, a tourist boomtown sells Chinese visitors a commoditized, politically palatable version of Tibetan culture.

item.title: Russia Probes Death of Woman Who Worked at Antiplague Institute
item.description: The Kremlin has sought to play down the death of the worker who contracted ”pneumonia of an unknown cause.”

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for October 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: These are the accounts that offer the best interest rates—without burdensome fees, gimmicks or other hassles

item.title: FBI Arrests Alleged Chinese Agent Accused of Spying on Son of Taiwan Leader
item.description: The alleged foreign agent was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport before she could board a flight to Shanghai.

item.title: Spanish Leader Calls for Elections, Riding Wave of Anger Over Housing Costs
item.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is gambling that outrage over soaring rents will help his socialist party secure a majority.

item.title: Shippers Are Offering Sailors Up to $25,000 a Trip to Sneak Oil Out of the Gulf
item.description: More tankers are getting through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iranian threats in a burgeoning system of risky shuttle runs that cost up to $40 million.

item.title: Afternoon Wake-ups and 1 a.m. Dinners: How F1 Drivers Beat Jet Lag
item.description: To stay sharp at the Singapore Grand Prix, drivers live in a nocturnal bubble. The big hurdles are social acceptability and sunlight.

item.title: Hormuz Gridlock Risks Global Food Crisis, International Chamber of Commerce Chief Says
item.description: Focus has been on the resulting rise in oil prices, but it is potential food shortages the world should be paying attention to, ICC secretary-general John Denton said.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Surges Past Lula, Setting Up a Bitter Brazil Election Runoff
item.description: The eldest son of imprisoned former President Jair Bolsonaro finished first, leaving the leftist incumbent with an uphill fight ahead of an Oct. 25 runoff.

item.title: Multiple Security Failures Allowed FlyDubai Pilot Into Cockpit
item.description: Authorities in three countries missed opportunities across the board; “there wasn’t proper vetting.”

item.title: All B-1 Bombers Returning to U.S. From U.K. Base
item.description: The withdrawal came amid security concerns around the base where several suspects were arrested last week in connection with a suspected plot.

item.title: Oil Was Pouring Out of Hormuz Again. Then Attacks on Ships Resurged.
item.description: Iran’s targeting of ships has improved, according to a U.S. official, making transits through the Strait of Hormuz riskier.

item.title: FlyDubai Attack Adds New Risks to Dubai’s War-Battered Economy
item.description: The attack was another blow to the emirate’s image as a haven insulated from the region’s turmoil, after the Iran war raised fears about flying to a city synonymous with luxury travel.

item.title: Japan Protests After U.S. Marine Accused of Murder
item.description: The killing risks rekindling tensions over the presence of the U.S. military on the Japanese island.

item.description: The arrival of the Bayeux Tapestry from France has sparked a class war in England.

item.title: The Death of the Old Middle East—and the Dangerous New World Replacing It
item.description: Simon Sebag-Montefiore on how traditional rivalries are receding as regional conflicts lead to powerful new alliances.

item.title: See What It’s Like to Be Under Fire in Kyiv, With 10 Air-Raid Alerts in 24 Hours
item.description: The dog on sedatives. The kindergartner who sleeps in the bathroom. The morning jog through the smoke. How Ukrainians are trying to keep life ordinary as drones and missiles rain down.

item.title: Lula Is the Brazilian Left’s Last Hope—And Its Biggest Problem
item.description: The 80-year-old president has crowded out successors. If he loses a re-election bid, it could shut his party out of power for years.

item.title: From a Love of Flying to a Midair Attack: What We Know About the FlyDubai Co-Pilot
item.description: Investigators want to know why Hamam Al-Hammami took a radical turn and why he was hired to fly a sensitive route between Dubai and Tel Aviv.

item.title: Netanyahu, in Tough Election Fight, Embraces Those Who Stopped FlyDubai Attack
item.description: The attack fits into the prime minister’s pitch that Israel is under attack from all sides and only his right-wing coalition can protect it.
